page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered for enterprise workloads that require high memory allocations alongside fast I/O throughput. Powered by 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processors on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading. The processor architecture includes 54 MB of Level 3 cache and supports vector and cryptographic extensions such as AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The platform provides 512 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-dense application environments.

Storage and networking resources are tightly integrated into the instance profile. The r6idn.16xlarge includes 3,800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance store volume, eliminating external EBS latency for applications reliant on high-speed scratch disks, buffering, or ephemeral transaction logs. Network capabilities are provisioned at a baseline throughput of 100 Gbps, ensuring consistent data transfer rates for distributed architectures, replication pools, and high-frequency data ingestion pipelines.

Performance testing reflects balanced compute output paired with exceptional domain-specific throughput. While stress-ng synthetic benchmarks place both single-core and multi-core CPU metrics within median ranges, the platform reaches the top quartile in PassMark database operations, encryption tests, and Clang compilation tasks. Redis workloads achieve up to 55.14 million operations per second, while static web serving achieves 45.56 GB per second. In machine learning inference evaluations, small and medium parameter models demonstrate competitive token generation speeds.

From a resource allocation standpoint, bundling 512 GB of RAM with nearly 4 TB of NVMe storage and 100 Gbps networking provides significant consolidation value for data-intensive applications. It mitigates the recurring costs and network overhead associated with provisioning detached block storage for caching layers. The r6idn.16xlarge is strategically deployed for production in-memory databases, distributed caching grids, transactional database backends, ETL data pipelines, and real-time big data analytics workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services r6idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized compute instance designed for memory-intensive workloads requiring rapid local I/O and high network throughput. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance runs on a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs with AVX-512 extensions. Memory capacity is substantial at 512 GB of DDR4 RAM, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Unlike diskless configurations, the r6idn.16xlarge integrates 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside 100 Gbps baseline networking. While stress-ng benchmarks indicate average baseline compute performance, the server demonstrates top-tier efficiency in PassMark database operations, Clang compilation, and cryptographic tests. The combination of dense memory, bundled high-speed solid-state storage, and elevated network capacity delivers strong hardware density for large in-memory databases, real-time big data analytics pipelines, and distributed cache infrastructure without requiring external network storage for local scratch disks.
